extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals and communications teams creating press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting, producing, and optimizing multimedia (images, video, graphics, interactive assets) to increase engagement and distribution of press releases. Covers which asset types to include, technical/rights requirements, SEO/formatting, and best production practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia elements significantly increase views and engagement for press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key claims on the page: 94% more views with multimedia elements; 650% increase in engagement with visuals; 6x higher engagement with multiple visual assets; 3x more interaction with video content; 48% increase in social sharing with immersive multimedia; 75% more likely to be shared with engaging visual content. Use these metrics to justify including multimedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Visuals substantially boost social platform engagement and interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics cited: 94% higher engagement on social platforms with visuals; Facebook posts with images see 53% more likes and 104% more comments; tweets with images receive about twice as many retweets. Tailor visuals for social sharing to amplify reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why visuals work (cognitive/shareability rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual content is processed faster and shared more frequently than text, making it more effective for audience attention and social sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims: visual content processed 60,000x faster than text in the brain; 40x more likely to be shared on social media; content with relevant images gets 94% more views. Use visuals to create immediate impressions and increase shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images vs. video
rubrics_metrics.description: Images are often more effective than video for press releases because they load faster and make an immediate impression, though video remains important to many marketers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes: images load faster and are easier to scan quickly; images make an immediate impression. However, 88% of video marketers say video is crucial. Consider trade-offs: use images for quick consumption and include short videos when depth or motion helps the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential multimedia types
rubrics_metrics.description: Core assets every press release should include: high-resolution product/event images, headshots of quoted executives, and company logos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labelled 'Essential' on the page — these assets are baseline requirements for media pickup and corporate branding. Ensure high resolution and correct branding usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended multimedia types
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental assets that improve storytelling: infographics for data stories, short videos (under 60 seconds), diagrams for complex topics, charts and graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labelled 'Recommended' — use these to illustrate data, explain complex ideas, and provide quick video summaries. Short videos should be concise (under 60 seconds) for higher engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced multimedia types
rubrics_metrics.description: High-production or interactive assets for greater pickup: B-roll for broadcast, interactive content, 3D visualizations, animated explainers, and embedded social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labelled 'Advanced' — useful for big announcements or when pursuing broadcast/interactive opportunities. Provide additional resolutions/formats for broadcasters and partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include at least one high-resolution image
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release should include at least one high-resolution image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit item in the 'Implicit Multimedia Rubric'. High resolution supports print and broadcast use; the page also recommends 300+ dpi for print. Provide multiple resolution options for different use cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption each image
rubrics_metrics.description: Every image should have an accompanying caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions explain context for media and help journalists quickly understand the asset. The 'Implicit Multimedia Rubric' lists captions as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide alt text for accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Include descriptive alt text for images to support accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the implicit rubric and reiterated in best practices ('Describe images with alt text'). Alt text also helps some search and accessibility compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer multiple resolution options
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide images and assets in multiple resolutions for different uses (web, print, broadcast).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit rubric: multiple resolution options ensure media can be used by various outlets. Include high-res (print/broadcast) and web-optimized versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleared for third-party distribution (usage rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: All multimedia must be cleared for third-party distribution and have clear copyright/usage rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit rubric and best practices emphasize clear copyright/usage rights and explicit clearance for distribution. Provide licensing/copyright statements with assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logos and branding clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Include clear company logos and consistent branding in assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit rubric requires logos and branding to be clear; ensure correct, high-quality logo files and brand-consistent imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include B-roll or video for broadcast pickup
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide B-roll or video assets to increase chances of broadcast coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit rubric and 'Advanced' types list B-roll and video for broadcasters. Supply appropriate formats, resolutions, and metadata for broadcast use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use schema markup for SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply schema markup to press releases and multimedia to improve discoverability and SEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit rubric lists schema markup for SEO. Mark up press release metadata and media where supported to increase search visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize file sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize multimedia file sizes so they load quickly while preserving quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit rubric and best practices: compress for web while preserving quality; images load faster than video. Balance quality and load time to maximize engagement and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide mobile-friendly formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure multimedia is in formats and sizes that display well on mobile devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit rubric lists mobile-friendly formats. Test assets on common mobile devices and consider aspect ratios and file sizes for mobile networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include images upfront (not as an afterthought)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place images early in the press release rather than appending them at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices: including images upfront increases immediate impact and scanning. Position key visuals near headlines or lead paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: High resolution (300+ dpi) for print
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide print-quality images at 300+ dpi when print usage is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices specifically call out 300+ dpi for print needs. Supply separate high-dpi files for print vs web versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard aspect ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver images in standard aspect ratios to ensure compatibility across platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices recommend standard ratios for predictable display on web, social, and broadcast. Provide crop-safe versions when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse representation in images
rubrics_metrics.description: Use images that show diverse representation appropriate to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices advise diverse representation to better reflect audiences and avoid bias. Prioritize authentic imagery that aligns with the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer real photos over stock when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Use real photography rather than stock imagery when feasible to increase authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices: real photos are recommended over stock to improve credibility. If stock is used, choose high-quality, relevant images and disclose where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear copyright/usage rights with assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state copyright and permitted uses for each multimedia asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices and implicit rubric stress clear usage rights so journalists and partners know redistribution permissions. Include credit lines and licensing details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compress for web while preserving quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Compress images and videos for web delivery but maintain acceptable visual quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices: use compression strategies to reduce load times but avoid over-compressing which degrades shareability and professional appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infographics for data stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Use infographics to present data-driven stories visually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended asset: infographics help make statistics and trends immediately understandable and shareable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short videos (under 60 seconds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include short videos — ideally under 60 seconds — to boost engagement without demanding long viewing time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended asset: short videos are more likely to be watched and shared. The page cites '3x more interaction with video content' so keep videos concise for higher interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagrams for complex topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide diagrams to simplify and explain complex subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended asset: diagrams help journalists and audiences grasp technical or complex information quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charts and graphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Include charts and graphs to visualize quantitative information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended asset: charts/graphs support data stories and can be adapted into infographics or social images for sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive content and advanced visualizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use interactive content, 3D visualizations, and animated explainers for high-value or technical announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'Advanced' — these assets can increase engagement and provide deeper understanding but require more production resources and compatibility considerations.
